facts.statement: Bohaiornis is the name of a genus of extinct animals.
facts.quote: genus: Bohaiornis

facts.statement: The only known species within the genus is Bohaiornis guoi.
facts.quote: species: guoi

facts.statement: The genus was described by Hu et al. in 2011.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Hu et al., 2011

facts.statement: Bohaiornis is classified within the class Aves.
facts.quote: classis: Aves

facts.statement: Bohaiornis belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: subclassis: Enantiornithes

facts.statement: Bohaiornis is the type genus of the family Bohaiornithidae.
facts.quote: familia: Bohaiornithidae

facts.statement: The authority for the genus name is Hu et al., 2011.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Hu et al., 2011

facts.statement: The species B. guoi was named by Hu et al. in 2011.
facts.quote: subdivision: B. guoi Hu et al., 2011

facts.statement: Fossils of Bohaiornis have been found in the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation in western Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of western Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Bohaiornis guoi was named by Dongyu Hu, Li Li, Lianhaim Hou, and Xing Xu in 2011.
facts.quote: The only known species, Bohaiornis guoi, was named by Dongyu Hu, Li Li, Lianhaim Hou and Xing Xu in 2011

facts.statement: The holotype specimen preserved two long, ribbon-like tail feathers instead of a fan of shorter feathers.
facts.quote: This specimen, LPM (Liaoning Paleontological Museum) B00167, preserved two long, ribbon-like feathers attached to the tail rather than a fan of shorter pennaceous feathers.

facts.statement: Bohaiornis was similar to Eoenantiornis but significantly larger in size.
facts.quote: It was similar to the slightly older Eoenantiornis, but much larger in size.

facts.statement: A second, larger specimen was described in 2014.
facts.quote: In 2014, a second, even larger specimen was described.

facts.statement: The second specimen preserved several rock-like structures inside the abdominal cavity.
facts.quote: and also preserved several rock-like structures within the abdominal cavity.

facts.statement: Researchers initially inferred these structures to be large, rough-textured gastroliths.
facts.quote: These were inferred to be large, rough-textured gastroliths.

facts.statement: Later analysis determined these structures were mineral concretions formed after death, not gastroliths.
facts.quote: However, these structures were later found to be mineral concretions which formed after the animal had already died.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Yixian Formation of the Lower Cretaceous in western Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han hallado en la formación Yixian del Cretácico Inferior del occidente de la provincia de Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The type and only known species, B. guoi, was named by Dongyu Hu, Li Li, Lianhaim Hou, and Xing Xu in 2011.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única conocida, B. guoi, fue denominada por Dongyu Hu, Li Li, Lianhaim Hou y Xing Xu en el año de 2011

facts.statement: The description was based on a well-preserved, fully articulated skeleton of a subadult individual.
facts.quote: sobre la base de un esqueleto bien preservado y totalmente articulado de un individuo subadulto.

facts.statement: A second specimen was described in 2014.
facts.quote: En 2014 se describió un segundo espécimen.

facts.statement: Bohaiornis lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Bohaiornis is the family Bohaiornithidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Bohaiornithidae

facts.statement: Bohaiornis belongs to the family Bohaiornithidae.
facts.quote: Family: Bohaiornithidae

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database classifies Bohaiornis under the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
